question: A 63-year-old man with no family history of prostatic carcinoma consulted for mild obstructive voiding symptoms. It provides a determination of prostate-specific antigen (PSA) less than 1 ng / mL. In rectal examination, a hardened and fixed area of ​​half a centimeter is seen in a prostatic lobe. In this case, the correct attitude is:

options.opa: Repeat the determination of PSA in three months.
options.opc: Treat with an alpha blocking to improve the obstructive symptomatology and repeat the PSA annually.

analysis: Given the findings of a hardened and fixed area on rectal examination in a patient with mild obstructive voiding symptoms and a PSA level less than 1 ng/mL, there is a high suspicion for prostate cancer. Immediate further evaluation is warranted to confirm the diagnosis.
